content.value_statement: Multi-agent systems can hide brittle handoffs, shared-state coupling, and unclear communication paths. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to map coordination models and produce a structured review.
actual_capabilities: Classifies systems as supervisor, peer-to-peer, pipeline, market-based, or hybrid coordination models.
Documents handoff mechanisms, context preservation, bidirectional control, and loop prevention.
Compares shared blackboard state with message passing and per-agent isolation.
Maps direct invocation, queue-based, and event-driven communication protocols.
Produces a reusable Markdown analysis template for framework reviews.
limitations: Does not execute, test, or validate agent framework code.
Requires the user to provide code paths, architecture notes, or relevant files.
Does not replace threat modeling for deployed agent systems.
Examples are illustrative and may need production security controls.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Map the coordination model, agent inventory, handoffs, and state boundaries in an existing codebase.

use_cases.title: Compare Framework Designs
use_cases.description: Evaluate how different frameworks route tasks, share state, and handle asynchronous communication.

use_cases.title: Plan Integration Work
use_cases.description: Identify where orchestration, queues, events, and loop prevention need attention before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Coordination Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a known agent system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this multi-agent system and classify its coordination model. Focus on control flow, agent roles, and handoff points.

prompt_templates.title: Map Handoffs and State
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review with source files available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the provided agent files. Document each handoff, what context moves between agents, and where state is shared or isolated.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Communication Protocols
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the communication protocols in these two multi-agent frameworks. Explain latency, coupling, async behavior, and failure modes for each.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Orchestration Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Full architecture review for a production candidate.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full multi-agent analysis for this codebase. Include coordination model, agent inventory, handoff mechanics, state sharing, communication protocol, loop prevention, and recommendations.

output_examples.input: Review an agent framework with one router and three specialist agents.
output_examples.output: The system uses a supervisor model. The router owns control flow, specialists receive delegated tasks, and failure handling depends on the router.

output_examples.input: Compare a queue-based pipeline with an event-driven agent network.
output_examples.output: The pipeline gives clearer ordering and simpler debugging. The event model reduces coupling but needs stronger observability and retry controls.

output_examples.input: Assess state sharing in a system with shared memory and per-agent queues.
output_examples.output: The design is hybrid. Shared memory improves context access, while queues preserve isolation for task messages and asynchronous replies.

best_practices: Provide representative orchestrator, router, and communication files before asking for analysis.
Ask for evidence locations so each coordination claim maps back to the source.
Review loop prevention, context preservation, and state isolation together.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for conclusions without sharing architecture details or code context.
Do not treat illustrative patterns as production-ready security designs.
Do not ignore error handling, retries, and handoff limits during analysis.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes agent coordination models, handoffs, shared state, and communication protocols.

faq.question: Can it compare different agent frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare routing, state sharing, communication style, and coordination tradeoffs.

faq.question: Does it run the agent system?
faq.answer: No. It reviews provided code and architecture context but does not execute the system.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide orchestrator files, agent definitions, routing logic, message queues, event handlers, and architecture notes.

faq.question: Can it find loop risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for loop prevention details such as depth limits, visited sets, and maximum handoffs.

faq.question: Is it useful for production reviews?
faq.answer: Yes, as an architecture review aid. It should be paired with testing, threat modeling, and operational review.
